title: Campaign: non-invasive brain measurement, applied current and weak magnetic fields
abstract: Subcampaign of 'how can human brain activity be measured without surgery, better than today?'. Scope: Methods that apply low-frequency electric current or weak magnetic fields and measure the tissue response: electrical impedance tomography, conductivity estimation and magnetic susceptometry. 22 papers. Status: bounds. Electrical impedance tomography of fast neural changes is blurred to 7 mm or more at 1 mA drive in a four-shell model and needs very long averaging; conductivity estimation from scalp data is often non-identifiable without extra information. Weak-field magnetic susceptometry fails with the scalp in air but could detect visual and hand-motor blocks in 10 min with tissue-matched water, 0.2 mm head motion and nanometre coil stability.
